Erin (Acme Sec): Hey team — we're blocked. Trying to view org audit logs in the console and getting a 403 with message 'missing entitlement: audit_log:read'. We use Okta SSO and our users have 'Security Reviewer' group mapped. Can someone help? I can reproduce: go to Console → Compliance → Audit logs -> 403. Screenshot: https://acme.screens/perm-403.png

Maya (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error text and the repro steps? Are other console areas working? do you see logs via API? :eyes:

Erin (Acme Sec): repro steps: 1) SSO login via Okta; 2) navigate: /console/org/ORG-12345/compliance/audit; 3) click "View Logs". Error modal says: "403 Forbidden — missing entitlement: audit_log:read". API check with my user token (via browser) also returns 403. Curl I ran from local:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <id_token_from_okta>" 
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/orgs/ORG-12345/audit/logs
# -> 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing entitlement: audit_log:read"}
```

Maya (Support): thanks. two quick checks: 1) can you confirm the SAML assertion from Okta has the entitlements claim? 2) are the users hitting this members of any admin group? sometimes the attribute mapping for SAML -> "entitlements" gets dropped. if you can, paste a (redacted) SAML samlResponse or the decoded JWT claims.

Erin (Acme Sec): i decoded the id_token and here's the relevant claims (redacted):

```json
{"sub":"erinx@acme.com","groups":["Security Reviewer"],"entitlements":["retention:90d"]}
```

so looks like audit_log:read is missing. Our Okta admin says we haven't set that entitlement on the group. But we thought the product docs said 'Security Reviewer' should map to audit read.

Maya (Support): okay that confirms it — this is a role-mapping/entitlement issue. Two separate bits: (A) the 'audit_log:read' permission controls UI/API read access; (B) 'retention:*' entitlements control how long logs are retained. they're independent. I'll loop in Eng-SRE and Security. @Devon can you confirm whether we also have any fallback policy that grants read to org owners?

Devon (Eng-SRE): joining. From the platform side, if the token doesn't include audit_log:read, we return 403. there is no graceful fallback for privacy reasons. quick check from our logs for ORG-12345 at 2026-06-05T14:02Z shows the auth decision:

```
REQUEST_ID=req-89a3
org=ORG-12345
principal=erinx@acme.com
claim.entitlements=["retention:90d"]
decision=DENY
reason=missing entitlement audit_log:read
```

so we need the entitlement in the SAML mapping or you need an admin-level API key temporarily. security, is adding entitlement straightforward?

SecurityOps: granting audit read is a change to entitlements mapping in our account provisioning (or in Okta attribute mapping). For customers using SSO we rely on an attribute called `entitlements` (string[]). The options:
- map the Okta group to include `audit_log:read` in the attribute; or
- we can issue a support-scoped org-admin API key for a short window while you update mapping (requires signed approval). Retention entitlements like `retention:90d` are independent; increasing retention does not give read access.

Maya (Support): Erin — easiest fix: have your Okta admin add `audit_log:read` to the entitlements attribute for the 'Security Reviewer' group. Example SAML attribute value we expect (in Okta profile mapping):

```json
["audit_log:read","retention:90d"]
```

If that's not possible immediately, we can spin a temporary org-admin API key for you (audit-only use). i'll open an internal escalation. Do you want us to do the API key?

Erin (Acme Sec): Okta admin wants a verification of exact attribute name and format. Also if we add audit_log:read will that automatically grant UI button in console? We don't want to give broader rights accidentally.

Devon (Eng-SRE): yes `audit_log:read` only gates read/listing of audit events; it does not grant write/or admin operations. Our console UI checks for that entitlement before showing the logs panel. Adding it to the entitlements array is safe for read-only access.

Maya (Support): i've created an internal support ticket: INC-54792 and pinged SecurityOps for the temporary key option. audits-bot: can you pull the last 7 days of auth decisions for ORG-12345 to attach?

audits-bot: Pull job started for org=ORG-12345 (7d range). ETA ~2m. Logs will be attached to INC-54792.

SecurityOps: For audit, here's the recommended Okta attribute mapping snippet to provide to your IdP admin:

```
Attribute name: entitlements
Format: JSON array of strings (UTF-8)
Example value: ["audit_log:read","retention:90d"]
```

Note: If your IdP cannot emit a JSON array, you can supply a comma-separated string and our SSO parser will accept it: `audit_log:read,retention:90d`.

Erin (Acme Sec): Okta admin updated the mapping to include audit_log:read as comma list. They say changed attribute for 'Security Reviewer' group at 2026-06-05T15:10Z. Confirmed SAML assertion now shows:

```json
{"sub":"erinx@acme.com","groups":["Security Reviewer"],"entitlements":["retention:90d","audit_log:read"]}
```

Maya (Support): thanks — give it a try, you may need to do a fresh SSO login (old session won't have new claims).

Erin (Acme Sec): fresh login done — I can see the Audit logs UI now and API access works too. :tada: closing out for us. Thanks everyone.

Maya (Support): awesome — marking INC-54792 resolved. A follow-up note: we'll update our docs with the comma-separated fallback example and add a troubleshooting snippet for '403 missing entitlement' pointing to the SSO mapping. I'll also add a small internal playbook step so support can issue the temporary key faster when needed. :memo:

Devon (Eng-SRE): filing a tiny telemetry tweak to include which attribute name was present in DENY logs to make this class of bug easier to debug next time (ENG-2104).

audits-bot: Incident INC-54792 updated: status=resolved, attachments=auth-decisions-ORG-12345-7d.log

Erin (Acme Sec): thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround!
